title: Service Call Allowance Under Cardinal Roadside Assistance: Periods, Use and Calls Beyond the Allowance
content:
Policy service desk guidance, Cardinal Roadside Assistance.

## Guidance

Each vehicle's Cardinal Roadside Assistance option has its own allowance of covered service calls per allowance period: the number of calls and the length of the period are those the option's benefit schedule sets. The allowance period starts on the option effective date and again on each anniversary of it. Calls are never pooled across the household's vehicles, and unused calls do not carry over where the option does not provide carryover.

A covered call is dispatched only while the vehicle has at least one call left in the current allowance period. Once the allowance is used, service is still dispatched, at the member's expense at the provider's rate, and recorded as a member charge.

One breakdown uses one call, even when several services are performed together.

## How the call balance moves

The calls left on an option are shown on the company's coverage record for that option, and that record, checked before dispatch, is what decides whether a covered call is available.

| Entry on the option | Effect on the calls left |
|---|---|
| Allowance granted for a new allowance period | Adds the calls of that period |
| Call restored on a dispatch | Adds one call back |
| Covered dispatch | Uses one call |

## Condition and result

| Calls left on the vehicle's option in the current allowance period | Result for the service requested |
|---|---|
| One or more | Dispatched as a covered call |
| None | Dispatched at the member's expense at the provider's rate, and recorded as a member charge |

## Hypothetical cases

1. **Household of two vehicles.** Car A's option shows no calls left; Car B's option shows two. Car A breaks down. Car B's calls cannot be used for Car A, because calls are not pooled across vehicles; Car A's service goes ahead at the member's expense at the provider's rate.
2. **Several services on one breakdown.** A vehicle with one call left needs a jump start and then a tow for the same breakdown. The breakdown uses one call.
3. **Period boundaries.** An option took effect on 10 March. Its allowance periods begin on 10 March of each year. Calls left unused on the day before 10 March do not pass into the period that begins on 10 March where the option provides no carryover.
4. **Last call.** A vehicle shows one call left. A covered call can be dispatched; after that dispatch the balance shows none, and a later breakdown in the same period is served at the member's expense.

Dates, vehicles and balances in these cases are illustrative.
